findings.documented: response field "token" carries the Bearer token
findings.actual: response field is "access_token"; there is no "token" key in the response
findings.how_found: inspected POST /auth/login response body
findings.impact: Frontend code reading response.token gets undefined and cannot authenticate

findings.documented: expires_in: 86400 — tokens valid for 24 hours
findings.actual: expires_in: 900 — tokens expire after 15 minutes
findings.how_found: inspected expires_in field in login response
findings.impact: Without token refresh, sessions break every 15 minutes instead of every 24 hours

findings.documented: user object: { email, name }
findings.actual: user object contains only { email }; name field is absent
findings.how_found: inspected user object in login response
findings.impact: Code displaying user.name renders undefined

findings.documented: API key as query parameter: ?api_key=IVY26-XXXX
findings.actual: API key must be in X-API-Key request header; query parameter rejected with 401 and message "send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter"
findings.how_found: sent api_key as URL query param; received 401
findings.impact: All documented curl examples using ?api_key= fail

findings.documented: Invalidates the current token server side
findings.actual: Tokens are stateless; server response: {"ok":true,"note":"tokens are stateless; discard them client side"}
findings.how_found: called POST /auth/logout and read response
findings.impact: Tokens cannot be revoked; logout is client-side only

findings.documented: limit parameter maximum: 200
findings.actual: limit is silently capped at 50; sending limit=200 or limit=999 both return limit=50
findings.how_found: sent limit=200, limit=999; response showed limit=50 in both cases
findings.impact: Extracting the full dataset requires 70 requests (3500/50) instead of the expected 17

findings.documented: page parameter (1-indexed) selects the page of results
findings.actual: page parameter is silently ignored; pagination works only via offset parameter
findings.how_found: page=2,limit=2 returned same listing_ids as offset=0,limit=2
findings.impact: Page-based iteration returns page 1 indefinitely

findings.documented: collection response shape: { total, page, page_size, results }
findings.actual: actual shape: { limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results } — has_more and offset replace page/page_size
findings.how_found: inspected all keys in collection response envelope
findings.impact: Code reading response.page or response.page_size gets undefined

findings.documented: total: exact number of records matching your filters
findings.actual: total underreports records: declared 3233 but 3500 records retrieved by following has_more to the end. Same pattern on /v1/rentals (declared 1219, fetched 1320) and /v1/projects (declared 370, fetched 400)
findings.how_found: paged through all pages until has_more=false; record count exceeded declared total
findings.impact: Stopping after ceil(total/limit) pages misses 267 listings, 101 rentals, and 30 projects

findings.documented: (project_id not documented as a filter)
findings.actual: project_id query parameter is silently ignored; ?project_id=P60096 returns all records unchanged
findings.how_found: sent ?project_id=P60096; got same total as unfiltered query
findings.impact: Listing counts per project must be computed client-side

findings.documented: sort_by accepts price, carpet_area, posted_at, bedroom with order=asc|desc
findings.actual: sort_by and order are silently ignored on all values tested (price, posted_at, bedroom); asc and desc return identical sequences
findings.how_found: compared first 5 listing_ids for sort_by=price asc vs desc, posted_at asc vs desc, bedroom asc vs desc — all three returned same order
findings.impact: No server-side sorting available; results are in default insertion order

findings.documented: Timestamps: ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix, everywhere in the API
findings.actual: posted_at has no timezone suffix (e.g. "2026-08-19T10:52:00"); server clock is IST (+05:30), so timestamps appear to be IST-local
findings.how_found: inspected posted_at values across many records; none end in Z or carry +05:30
findings.impact: Date range queries treating posted_at as UTC will be 5h30m off

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} — single listing detail
findings.actual: returns 404 Not Found; correct path uses plural: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}
findings.impact: All code using documented singular path silently gets 404

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar — up to 10 comparable listings
findings.actual: returns 404 Not Found
findings.how_found: called the endpoint with valid listing_id and auth
findings.impact: "Similar listings" feature cannot be implemented via this endpoint

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary — pre-computed city-level aggregates
findings.actual: returns 404 Not Found
findings.how_found: called the endpoint with valid auth
findings.impact: Insights/analytics screen has no endpoint to call

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites, DELETE /v1/favourites/{id}
findings.actual: GET /v1/favourites returns 404 Not Found
findings.how_found: called GET /v1/favourites with valid auth
findings.impact: Saved/favourites feature has no working endpoint

findings.documented: listing object schema does not mention is_live field
findings.actual: every listing record includes is_live (boolean) — true for active listings, false for inactive/withdrawn
findings.how_found: inspected listing record field keys in API response
findings.impact: is_live is the only way to filter active listings and is critical for assignment answers

findings.documented: rental object schema does not mention is_live field
findings.actual: every rental record includes is_live (boolean)
findings.how_found: inspected rental record field keys
findings.impact: Rental filtering by active status is possible but undocumented

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees
findings.actual: price_min and price_max are NOT in rupees. Values range from 1 to 99 — consistent with crores (for values < 10) and lakhs (for values > 50). No project has a price value in the millions that rupees would require. 184 of 400 projects show price_min > price_max numerically, which is explained by price_min stored in lakhs and price_max in crores.
findings.how_found: cross-referenced project price_max against actual listing prices for same project; all values < 100, none in rupee scale
findings.impact: Cannot compute accurate price ranges or find costliest project without knowing the unit

findings.documented: returns active, valid listings
findings.actual: 18 records describe something that cannot exist: negative prices (5 records: 100-6001461, 100-6002071, DWE-6002663, MAG-6000631, SQU-6003044, ZER-6000669), floor > total_floors (6 records), carpet_area > super_built_up_area (7 records). Area anomalies in magichomes records (likely sqm/sqft mislabelling) are a separate data quality issue but not logically impossible.
findings.how_found: systematic validation of all 3500 listing records against physical constraints
findings.impact: Corrupt records must be excluded from price/area calculations

findings.documented: every listing_id is globally unique; each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property
findings.actual: one physical property is described by two records from different sources: MAG-6000753 (magichomes) and DWE-6003269 (dwelling) share the same apartment_name, locality, floor, bedroom, carpet_area, latitude and longitude
findings.how_found: grouped all 3500 records by (apartment_name, locality, floor, bedroom, carpet_area); found one group with 2 records
findings.impact: unique_properties count = 3499, not 3500

findings.documented: listings are posted by genuine owners or agents
findings.actual: 230 listings share phone numbers across multiple different seller names. 12 phone numbers each appear under 2-6 different posted_by_name values (e.g. +912009782693 appears as Shreya Iyer, Nisha Kulkarni, Varun Verma, and Suresh Nair across 35 listings in different localities). A real person has one name; one contact number used under many distinct names is a hallmark of fake listings generated to collect enquiries.
findings.how_found: grouped all listing records by posted_by_contact; flagged contacts where the set of posted_by_name values had 2 or more distinct entries
findings.impact: 230 fake listings inflate enquiry volume and mislead buyers
